column2: Rationale / Explanation

Prevents compromised agents from running indefinitely with stolen credentials. Agents use short-lived OAuth2/OIDC tokens (1-4 hour expiry) that auto-refresh through identity brokers.

Check:
• Token expiration settings in identity provider
• Automatic refresh mechanism exists
• No permanent API keys in agent configs

Common mistake: Using API keys valid for months instead of expiring tokens.

Ask: Engineering/DevOps team

AI agents can execute thousands of operations per minute—far beyond human capacity. Specialized SIEM rules detect when agents are compromised or behaving abnormally.

Check:
• AI agent identities tagged in SIEM
• Alert rules for velocity anomalies (requests/minute)
• Alerts for unusual access patterns/times

Ask: Security Operations/SOC team

Eliminates standing privileges that could be exploited. Agents start with zero permissions and receive only exact access needed for each task, then lose it immediately.

Check:
• Agents have no default permissions when idle
• Temporary permissions granted per task
• Automatic permission revocation after use

Common mistake: Giving agents broad permanent permissions for convenience.

Ask: IAM/Security team

Catches prompt injection attacks before they reach your main AI model—like security screening before entering a building. Fast, lightweight SLMs detect malicious patterns (jailbreaks, encoded attacks).

Check:
• Filtering layer exists before main LLM
• Architecture diagrams show security component
• SLM classifier or commercial prompt firewall deployed

Ask: AI Engineering team

Prevents attackers from using AI responses to reverse-engineer private training data or determine if specific individuals' data was used in training—critical for privacy compliance.

Check:
• Output filters scan for data leakage patterns
• Detection of repeated extraction queries
• Monitoring for statistical inference attempts

Common mistake: Only filtering obvious PII, missing sophisticated extraction attacks.

Ask: AI Security/Data Privacy team

Protects expensive API credentials from theft. Secure gateway/proxy handles authentication behind the scenes so agents and users never see actual API keys.

Check:
• Credentials stored in secure vault (AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault)
• API keys NOT in code, environment variables, or logs
• Backend service injects credentials, not frontend

Ask: Engineering/Platform team

Prevents AI agents from being tricked into attacking your internal network. Without SSRF protection, malicious prompts could make AI send requests to internal servers or cloud metadata services.

Check:
• URL/API allowlist for permitted external services
• Blocking of private IP ranges (10.x, 192.168.x, 127.0.0.1)
• Cloud metadata endpoints blocked

Ask: Security/Network team

Ensures agents only access resources relevant to their current task. If summarizing Invoice_A, agent shouldn't access Invoice_B or payroll data, even with general "read" permission.

Check:
• Access controls verify task/session context
• API calls include task identifiers
• Authorization checks "Is data related to current task?"

Ask: Engineering/IAM team

Prevents attackers from poisoning the AI's tools. Compromised calculators, converters, or connectors make all AI outputs unreliable or malicious.

Check:
• Tools have digital signatures or checksums
• Tool registry with approved versions
• System rejects unsigned/modified tools

Common mistake: Installing plugins from GitHub without verifying authenticity.

Ask: AI Engineering/Security team

Ensures humans waiting for real-time AI responses don't experience delays because batch jobs are consuming all compute resources.

Check:
• Network/load balancer has traffic prioritization rules
• Separate queues for interactive vs. batch workloads
• Interactive requests maintain <2sec response during batch processing

Ask: Infrastructure/DevOps team

Prevents GPU starvation and cost overruns by adjusting rate limits based on actual token costs. Different models have different pricing—GPT-4 costs more than GPT-3.5, and output tokens typically cost more than input tokens.

Check:
• Rate limits adjust based on model token pricing
• Global FinOps quotas enforced across all users
• Input/output tokens tracked separately
• Per-user fairness maintained

Ask: Engineering/FinOps team

Saves costs by automatically downgrading to cheaper models when budgets are exhausted. Instead of blocking users when premium tokens run out, system routes to smaller, less expensive models.

Check:
• Auto-routing logic to cheaper models exists
• Seamless user experience during downgrade
• Cost thresholds trigger model switching

Common mistake: Blocking all AI access instead of degrading gracefully to cheaper models.

Ask: Engineering/FinOps team

Prevents legal liability from using unlicensed or non-consented data in training. Using data without proper rights can invalidate your model and trigger regulatory penalties.

Check:
• Legal rights verification before ingestion
• User consent validation automated
• Third-party license metadata checked (Hugging Face, etc.)
• Rejection of data without proper rights

Ask: Legal/Data Governance team

Enables regulatory audits by tracing any AI output back to its source training data. Critical for proving compliance when regulators question how a model reached a specific decision.

Check:
• Cryptographic signatures link outputs to model versions
• Model versions linked to exact training datasets
• Raw data provenance fully documented
• 72-hour audit response capability

Ask: Data Governance/Compliance team

Blocks unauthorized third-party data lacking proper consent/licensing. Schema enforcement with cryptographic signatures ensures only properly authorized data enters your systems.

Check:
• API boundary enforces schema validation
• Cryptographic signatures required on consents/licenses
• Automatic rejection of unsigned payloads
• Third-party data pre-validated

Ask: Engineering/Legal team

Creates tamper-proof audit trail of all dataset modifications. Append-only logs prevent anyone—including admins—from hiding changes to training data after the fact.

Check:
• Distributed ledger or append-only log implemented
• All manual changes recorded immutably
• Logs cannot be edited or deleted
• Timestamps and user IDs captured

Ask: Data Engineering/Security team

Prevents prompt injection attacks by separating system instructions from user input at the token level. Ensures users cannot override system prompts with malicious instructions.

Check:
• System and user tokens technically separated
• Separation enforced, not just logical
• Detection of system prompt injection attempts
• Token-level classification implemented

Ask: AI Security/Engineering team

Detects and blocks jailbreak attempts where users try to bypass safety filters. Common jailbreak patterns include "ignore previous instructions" or encoded attack prompts.

Check:
• Automated jailbreak detection deployed
• Known jailbreak patterns blocked
• Intent classification identifies bypass attempts
• Regular updates to jailbreak signatures

Ask: AI Security team

Provides graceful failure when AI systems timeout or malfunction. Instead of showing errors to users, system returns safe, pre-written responses maintaining user experience.

Check:
• Circuit breakers configured for LLM failures
• Canned responses prepared for common failures
• User sees safe fallback, not error messages
• Timeout thresholds defined

Ask: Engineering/DevOps team

Prevents sensitive data leakage in real-time AI outputs. Token-by-token inspection catches PII, secrets, or confidential data before it reaches users.

Check:
• DLP proxy intercepts LLM output streams
• Token-level scanning for sensitive patterns
• Real-time blocking of sensitive data
• SSNs, API keys, credit cards detected

Ask: Security/DLP team

Protects PII by redacting locally without sending to third-party APIs. Using local NER models ensures sensitive data never leaves your environment during cleaning.

Check:
• NER models hosted on-premises or in private cloud
• PII redaction happens before external transmission
• No sensitive data sent to third-party APIs
• Local processing verified

Common mistake: Using external APIs for PII detection, exposing data during the cleaning process.

Ask: Data Privacy/Engineering team

Defines response plan when sensitive data bypasses filters. Even best filters aren't 100% perfect—having automated mitigation for breaches is critical.

Check:
• Automated incident response for filter bypasses
• Data breach notification procedures
• Immediate containment actions defined
• Post-incident analysis process

Ask: Security/Incident Response team

Prevents user data from being executed as code by the model. Control plane (commands) and data plane (user content) separation ensures malicious inputs can't trigger unintended model behaviors.

Check:
• Network-level separation enforced
• User data cannot reach control plane
• Strict API boundaries between planes
• Architecture diagrams show separation

Ask: Engineering/Security team

Removes hidden attacks in RAG documents before AI processing. Invisible Unicode characters or steganographic instructions can manipulate AI behavior without visible text changes.

Check:
• Content sanitization before context window insertion
• Unicode normalization applied
• Steganographic pattern detection
• All retrieved documents processed

Common mistake: Trusting document content from trusted sources without sanitization.

Ask: AI Security team

Tracks detection accuracy and defines response actions. Knowing false positive/negative rates helps tune detection systems and ensures appropriate responses when threats are detected.

Check:
• False positive/negative rates documented
• Regular metrics updates
• Clear action plans for detection hits
• Escalation procedures defined

Ask: Security Operations team

Adapts to evolving attack patterns instead of relying on static rules. Unsupervised learning detects novel poisoning attempts that static rules would miss.

Check:
• Unsupervised learning calibrates thresholds
• Dynamic baseline adjustments
• Detection of slow-burn coordinated attacks
• Regular recalibration performed

Common mistake: Using only static thresholds that attackers can learn to evade.

Ask: Data Science/Security team

Protects privacy by removing PII before it reaches AI systems. Pre-ingestion buffer automatically redacts sensitive data, preventing it from being stored or processed.

Check:
• Automatic PII redaction before storage
• SSN, credit card, email masking
• Prompt data minimized before RAG ingestion
• Privacy buffer in architecture

Ask: Data Privacy/Engineering team

Isolates web scraping to prevent malware from reaching corporate networks. Disposable sandbox ensures any malicious payload dies when sandbox is destroyed.

Check:
• Web scraping in isolated sandbox
• Ephemeral/disposable environment used
• No network path to corporate intranet
• Sandbox destroyed after each scrape

Ask: Security/Infrastructure team

Prevents employees from pasting sensitive data into public AI tools. DLP agents intercept and block classified code or financial data from being sent to ChatGPT, Claude, etc.

Check:
• DLP agents on endpoints configured
• Blocking of classified data to AI interfaces
• Real-time interception of paste operations
• Alerts when blocking occurs

Ask: Security/IT Operations team

Ensures training data integrity through immutability and audit trails. Quarantine, WORM storage, and transparent logging prevent data tampering or unauthorized modifications.

Check:
• Schema violations trigger automatic quarantine
• WORM storage for gold-standard datasets
• Immutable audit trails of all changes
• Pipeline modifications logged

Ask: Data Engineering/Governance team

Prevents runaway AI costs from infinite loops or unexpected behavior. Automated shutdowns protect budget when agents consume excessive tokens or enter recursive patterns.

Check:
• Token velocity monitoring in real-time
• Cost-per-resolution tracking
• Auto-termination on anomalies
• Circuit breakers for recursive loops

Ask: Engineering/FinOps team

Protects model weights from compromised infrastructure. TEEs process encrypted models in isolated memory, preventing even hypervisor-level attacks from accessing weights.

Check:
• Trusted Execution Environments deployed
• Model weights encrypted in memory
• Protection from compromised hypervisor
• Intel SGX, AMD SEV, or similar used

Ask: Infrastructure/Security team

Enforces data residency requirements by preventing cross-border replication. Hard geofencing ensures AI data stays within legal jurisdiction, critical for GDPR, data sovereignty laws.

Check:
• Geographic replication blocked at infrastructure level
• Data residency rules enforced
• Cross-border transfers prevented
• Jurisdiction boundaries hard-coded

Ask: Infrastructure/Compliance team

Ensures data remains encrypted until authorized users request it. HYOK/CMK with identity-based decryption means stolen data is useless without proper authentication.

Check:
• Customer-managed encryption keys (CMK)
• Identity-based decryption enforced
• Keys remain under customer control
• Decryption only on verified access

Ask: Security/Infrastructure team

Prevents ransomware and admin compromise from deleting training data. Object Lock mathematically guarantees immutability—even admins can't delete until retention expires.

Check:
• AWS S3 Object Lock or equivalent enabled
• Retention policies at bucket level
• Immutability enforced, not optional
• Protection against compromised credentials

Ask: Cloud Infrastructure team

Protects vector databases from reconstruction attacks. Logical isolation and PIR technology prevent attackers from inferring original data through similarity queries.

Check:
• Vector database isolated from public APIs
• Private Information Retrieval implemented
• Inference-based attacks mitigated
• Network segmentation enforced

Ask: AI Security/Infrastructure team

Prevents data leakage between training and test sets. Separate transformations and entropy monitoring ensure test data doesn't contaminate training, and crucial information isn't lost.

Check:
• Training/test transformations strictly separated
• Information entropy monitored
• No data leakage between sets
• Compression doesn't strip critical nuances

Ask: Data Science/ML Engineering team

Prevents SMOTE from creating unrealistic synthetic minorities. Strict auditing ensures over-sampling doesn't introduce hallucinated data that misrepresents underrepresented groups.

Check:
• SMOTE usage audited for accuracy
• Synthetic samples validated against real data
• Hallucination detection for minority classes
• Regular quality reviews

Ask: Data Science team

Tests whether embeddings can leak original PII. Mathematical reversibility testing ensures transformed data can't be reverse-engineered to reconstruct sensitive information.

Check:
• Embedding reversibility testing performed
• PII reconstruction attempts blocked
• Mathematical proofs of irreversibility
• Regular testing for new embedding methods

Ask: Data Science/Security team

Distinguishes real data from imputed guesses. Boolean flags tell the model which values are actual measurements vs. filled-in missing data, preventing false confidence.

Check:
• Imputation flags appended to feature vectors
• Model can distinguish empirical vs. imputed
• Attention mechanism informed of data quality
• All NULL imputations tracked

Ask: Data Science team

Ensures identical pipeline runs produce identical results. Deterministic reproducibility is critical for audits, debugging, and proving model compliance.

Check:
• Deterministic ETL processes enforced
• Same inputs always produce same outputs
• Mathematical reproducibility verified
• Pipeline version control maintained

Ask: Data Engineering team

Removes adversarial noise designed to manipulate models. Input sanitization strips hidden characters or patterns that could trigger attacks or bypass filters.

Check:
• Hidden character stripping implemented
• Adversarial noise detection
• Input normalization before processing
• Pattern-based attack filtering

Ask: AI Security team

Verifies embeddings preserve original data meaning. Mutual Information scores mathematically prove vectorization didn't lose critical structural information.

Check:
• Automated MI score calculation
• Verification that meaning preserved
• Structural information loss detection
• Regular embedding quality checks

Ask: Data Science team

Proves which context was used for specific AI responses. Immutable RAG logs enable audits showing exactly what information the AI accessed during inference.

Check:
• RAG context injection logged immutably
• Logs cannot be altered after creation
• Specific inference events traceable
• Regulatory audit capability

Ask: Engineering/Compliance team

Detects schema changes instantly instead of overnight. Real-time Kafka streaming ensures data catalog stays current with immediate notifications of structural changes.

Check:
• Kafka or similar event bus integrated
• Real-time schema change notifications
• No reliance on batch scans
• Instant propagation to catalog

Ask: Data Engineering team

Automatically adjusts access when data sensitivity changes. Dynamic IAM ensures access is immediately revoked if datasets are reclassified to higher sensitivity tiers.

Check:
• IAM policies tied to metadata tags
• Auto-revocation on reclassification
• Real-time access adjustments
• No manual permission updates needed

Ask: IAM/Data Governance team

Assigns human accountability for AI data quality. Stewards with mandatory review ensure high-risk models only ingest quality-validated data, preventing garbage-in-garbage-out.

Check:
• Every AI dataset has assigned steward
• Mandatory human review for quality exceptions
• Mature data quality governance practices
• Exception approval before high-risk ingestion

Ask: Data Governance team

Discovers hidden PII and tracks synthetic data automatically. Automated scanning finds shadow PII humans might miss and flags when knowledge becomes outdated.

Check:
• Automated PII discovery scanning
• Shadow PII detection beyond obvious fields
• Synthetic/imputed values tagged
• Stale metadata flagged on schema changes

Ask: Data Governance/Privacy team

Enforces data usage restrictions across all systems. Embedded policies like "Do not use for credit scoring" stay with data and are programmatically enforced, not just documented.

Check:
• Usage policies in metadata, not separate docs
• Policies persist across cloud systems
• Programmatic enforcement, not manual
• Automatic blocking of policy violations

Ask: Data Governance/Engineering team

Prevents alert fatigue from outdated baselines. Rolling baselines adapt to normal changes, reducing false positives while detecting genuine drift.

Check:
• Dynamic rolling baselines vs. static
• Continuous calibration of drift detection
• Alert fatigue mitigation
• Baseline updates match business changes

Ask: ML Operations/Data Science team

Enables rapid legal hold on training data. Automated e-Discovery capability can instantly freeze and extract relevant data subsets when litigation begins.

Check:
• Automated legal hold capability exists
• Training data subset extraction possible
• Freeze mechanisms in place
• Compliance with e-Discovery requirements

Ask: Legal/IT team

Prevents model collapse from synthetic data loops. Quality gates ensure AI-generated data doesn't accidentally become training input, causing recursive degradation.

Check:
• Quality gates prevent synthetic loops
• AI-generated data tagged and tracked
• Automatic blocking of synthetic training data
• Loop detection mechanisms

Ask: Data Engineering/ML team

Quarantines bad data until human approval. Cryptographic locks prevent anomalous data from reaching training pipelines without documented human sign-off.

Check:
• Automatic routing to quarantine queue
• Cryptographic locks on quarantined data
• Human sign-off required for release
• Audit trail of approval decisions

Ask: Data Engineering/Governance team

Evaluates access based on current context and risk, not static roles. Zero Trust with metadata filtering prevents inappropriate data access and cross-tenant leakage.

Check:
• Dynamic access evaluation vs. static roles
• User intent and risk assessed continuously
• Metadata filtering enforces boundaries
• Cross-tenant retrieval prevented

Ask: IAM/Security team

Tests data pipeline robustness against edge cases. Adversarial perturbations verify cleaning logic handles unusual inputs without breaking or introducing bias.

Check:
• Adversarial inputs in testing framework
• Edge case robustness verified
• Pipeline tested against perturbations
• Mathematical robustness proven

Ask: Data Engineering/QA team

Enforces data tags at OS/hypervisor level. MAC ensures tags persist regardless of application bugs or compromises, providing defense-in-depth.

Check:
• Mandatory Access Control at OS level
• Tags enforced below application layer
• Hypervisor-level enforcement
• Application bypasses prevented

Ask: Infrastructure/Security team

Creates encryption keys only when needed, for specific API calls. Ephemeral KMS keys tied to OAuth tokens minimize exposure window if credentials leak.

Check:
• Keys minted only per API call
• OAuth token mapping to encryption keys
• Ephemeral keys auto-expire
• No long-lived encryption keys

Ask: Security/Infrastructure team

Redacts PII before AI agents see database rows. Active DLP proxy automatically masks sensitive fields, preventing agents from ingesting raw PII.

Check:
• DLP/masking proxy in query path
• Automatic PII redaction before agent access
• Real-time masking, not post-processing
• Database queries routed through proxy

Ask: Security/Data Privacy team

Exhausts botnet resources through cryptographic challenges. Proof-of-Work or client attestation makes automated scraping computationally expensive, protecting API endpoints.

Check:
• Cryptographic PoW challenges at API edge
• Client attestation required
• Botnet resource exhaustion design
• Rate limiting augmented with crypto challenges

Ask: Security/Infrastructure team

Blocks indirect prompt injections from external sources. Prompt firewall inspects RAG-retrieved content and web search results for malicious instructions before model processing.

Check:
• Prompt firewall/inspection proxy deployed
• External content inspected before model
• Indirect injection detection
• RAG and web search content validated

Ask: AI Security team

Limits blast radius of compromised tokens. Minute-expiry with geographic restrictions ensures stolen tokens are useless quickly and from wrong locations.

Check:
• Token expiration measured in minutes
• Geographic/IP restrictions enforced
• Clean termination even during long tasks
• Automatic token rotation

Ask: Security/Engineering team

Prevents exploitation of deprecated API parameters. Schema validation automatically rejects requests attempting to use undocumented or old endpoint parameters.

Check:
• API gateway enforces schema validation
• Automatic rejection of invalid requests
• Deprecated parameters blocked
• Schema versioning enforced

Ask: API/Security team

Monitors and blocks unauthorized data transfers. Comprehensive DLP prevents models from exfiltrating massive datasets or pulling more data than requested.

Check:
• DLP on AI inputs and outputs
• Egress data inspection active
• Massive transfer blocking
• Row-count validation (requested vs. pulled)

Ask: Security/DLP team

Routes anomalous inputs to humans instead of risking hallucinations. Safe degradation ensures questionable inputs get human review rather than unreliable AI responses.

Check:
• Automated HITL queue routing on drift
• Safe degradation protocol defined
• Anomalous inputs flagged for review
• Hallucination prevention priority

Ask: ML Operations/Engineering team

Traces hallucinations back to root cause data issues. Automated RCA scripts map problematic outputs to specific poisoned or degraded data nodes enabling rapid fixes.

Check:
• Automated RCA capability deployed
• Hallucination-to-data mapping
• Immediate root cause identification
• Poisoned node detection

Ask: Data Engineering/ML Operations team

Prevents infinite reasoning loops in multi-agent systems. Graph-cycle detection identifies and halts agents stuck in circular logic patterns.

Check:
• Deterministic cycle detection implemented
• Multi-agent chain monitoring
• Automatic loop termination
• Graph analysis of reasoning patterns

Ask: AI Engineering team

Prevents AI from using outdated business data. TTL flags ensure embeddings automatically expire, preventing the model from reasoning on functionally deprecated information.

Check:
• TTL expiry flags in embeddings
• Automatic expiration of old data
• Deprecated data unretrievable
• Temporal validity enforced

Ask: Data Engineering/ML team

Ensures AI actions match user intent. Semantic monitoring validates agent actions (sending emails, executing transactions) strictly align with original requests and policy boundaries.

Check:
• Intent-action matching validation
• Original request vs. action comparison
• Policy envelope enforcement
• Autonomous action boundaries defined

Ask: AI Security/Governance team

Detects bias introduction from pipeline updates. Hourly automated testing with gold standard suite ensures changes don't create new fairness issues.

Check:
• Automated bias test suite exists
• Hourly execution frequency
• Gold standard test cases maintained
• Pipeline update validation

Ask: ML Operations/Data Science team

Provides unified visibility across all systems. Integration into central observability platform (OpenTelemetry) prevents monitoring silos and enables correlation with other infrastructure.

Check:
• AI monitoring in central dashboard
• OpenTelemetry or similar integration
• No siloed monitoring tools
• Cross-system correlation enabled

Ask: DevOps/SRE team

Protects against hardware side-channel attacks. Mitigations prevent GATEBLEED and similar attacks that leak training data through power consumption patterns.

Check:
• Hardware mitigations for side-channels
• GATEBLEED protections deployed
• Power-gating attack prevention
• GPU/TPU security features enabled

Ask: Infrastructure/Security team

Ensures adequate serving capacity for production use. Most AI value comes from inference, not training—allocating 75%+ for serving ensures models can actually be used.

Check:
• Compute budget allocation reviewed
• Over 75% allocated to inference
• Production serving capacity adequate
• Training vs. serving balance maintained

Ask: FinOps/Infrastructure team

Enables rapid failover during GPU shortages. Alternative cluster or on-prem hardware access in under 48 hours prevents extended outages during supply constraints.

Check:
• Alternative GPU cluster identified
• Sub-48-hour failover capability tested
• On-premises hardware option exists
• Switching procedures documented

Ask: Infrastructure/BCDR team

Prevents training data leakage via power analysis. Hardware-level mitigations stop side-channel attacks that extract data by monitoring power fluctuations.

Check:
• Hardware-level side-channel mitigations
• Power fluctuation attack prevention
• Physical security for training infrastructure
• Monitoring for anomalous power patterns

Ask: Infrastructure/Security team

Maximizes GPU utilization through sharing. Dynamic partitioning allows multiple small tasks to share one GPU instead of wasting resources with full-GPU-per-job allocation.

Check:
• GPU sharing/partitioning enabled
• Dynamic allocation vs. static
• Multi-tenant GPU usage
• Utilization metrics tracked

Ask: Infrastructure/FinOps team

Prevents compromised firmware from running on GPUs. Cryptographic signature verification on every boot ensures only authorized firmware executes.

Check:
• Firmware signature verification at boot
• Cryptographic validation implemented
• Unauthorized firmware rejected
• Boot-time security checks

Ask: Infrastructure/Security team

Prevents runaway costs from unlimited tool use. Hard step limits cap the number of tool invocations per agent session, protecting budget and preventing infinite loops.

Check:
• Maximum step boundaries in system prompts
• Hard limits vs. soft warnings
• Per-session tool invocation caps
• Cost protection enforced

Ask: Engineering/FinOps team

Optimizes for different workload requirements. Separate architectures for inference (low latency) and training (high throughput) maximize efficiency for each use case.

Check:
• Separate inference and training architectures
• Inference optimized for latency
• Training optimized for throughput
• Architecture matches workload needs

Ask: Infrastructure/ML Engineering team

Accelerates data movement with direct GPU access. RDMA bypasses CPU bottlenecks, moving data directly from storage to GPU memory for faster processing.

Check:
• RDMA implementation for GPU data transfers
• CPU bypass configured
• Direct storage-to-GPU paths
• Network infrastructure supports RDMA

Ask: Infrastructure/Network team

Enables fast checkpoint ingestion without training disruption. Sub-60-second loading of terabyte checkpoints allows rapid recovery or experimentation without cluster pauses.

Check:
• Checkpoint ingestion under 60 seconds
• No training cluster pauses required
• Storage bandwidth adequate for terabytes
• Parallel loading capability

Ask: Infrastructure/ML Engineering team

Enables independent scaling of storage capacity and performance to optimize costs and flexibility. Disaggregated storage architecture allows you to add petabytes of capacity without paying for additional compute IOPS you don't need, or boost performance without buying unnecessary storage. This is critical for AI workloads where data volume and processing needs often scale at different rates—your training dataset might grow 10x while compute requirements remain stable, or vice versa. Traditional coupled architectures force you to overprovision and waste money on resources you'll never use.

Check:
• Storage capacity scales independently from compute
• IOPS performance adjustable without storage changes
• Cost optimization through separate scaling
• Architecture supports petabyte-scale growth

Ask: Infrastructure/Storage team

Enables secure data sharing across AI teams without costly duplication or data silos. Data Mesh architecture allows different AI domains (marketing, finance, operations) to query shared datasets with version control, lineage tracking, and access controls—all without physically copying terabytes of data into each team's environment. This prevents the common problem where each team maintains separate copies of customer data, creating synchronization nightmares, storage waste, and compliance risks. Federated queries with proper governance mean one authoritative data source serves all AI initiatives.

Check:
• Federated domains can query shared datasets
• No physical data duplication required
• Dataset versioning and lineage tracked
• Cross-domain access controls enforced

Ask: Data Architecture/Engineering team

Prevents catastrophic cloud bills from data exfiltration or misconfigurations. Automated egress termination acts as a financial circuit breaker—if outbound data transfer costs suddenly spike (which could indicate a breach, misconfigured job, or ransomware exfiltrating data), the system instantly cuts network egress to prevent runaway charges. Without this, organizations have woken up to six-figure surprise bills from compromised systems transferring petabytes out of the cloud. This is both a security control and a cost-protection mechanism.

Check:
• Billing alerts configured for egress costs
• Automatic network egress termination on spikes
• Anomaly thresholds defined and tested
• Alert-to-action automation in place

Common mistake: Having alerts but no automated response, requiring manual intervention that may come too late.

Ask: FinOps/Cloud Infrastructure team

Optimizes storage performance and costs through intelligent tiering. NVMe-over-Fabrics provides ultra-fast access to active training data (low latency, high IOPS), while automated tiering moves completed models and archived datasets to cheap cold storage. This prevents paying premium NVMe prices for data you rarely access. Think of it like keeping today's work on your desk (NVMe-oF) and filing completed projects in the basement (object storage)—you need both, but shouldn't pay desk-space prices for everything.

Check:
• NVMe-oF deployed for hot training data
• Automated tiering to cold storage configured
• Tiering policies based on access patterns
• Cost savings from tiering measured

Ask: Infrastructure/Storage team

Minimizes network latency in distributed training by reducing physical distance between nodes. Distributed AI training requires constant synchronization between GPUs—placing nodes physically close together on the same rack or network segment dramatically reduces communication time, speeding up training and preventing stragglers. Poor placement can make a 10-node training job run slower than 5 optimally-placed nodes. Automatic placement by interconnect distance ensures your orchestrator always chooses the fastest configuration.

Check:
• Orchestrator considers physical interconnect distance
• Automatic node placement for distributed jobs
• Network topology awareness in scheduling
• Training speed improvements measurable

Ask: Infrastructure/ML Platform team

Prevents resource exhaustion and security violations through automated policy enforcement. Admission controllers act as gatekeepers—blocking any AI container that lacks proper resource limits (preventing one job from starving others) or required security tags (preventing unvetted code from running). Without this, a single poorly-configured job can consume all cluster resources, or malicious code can deploy without security review. This is your last line of defense before workloads hit production infrastructure.

Check:
• Kyverno, OPA, or similar admission controller deployed
• Resource limit requirements enforced
• Security tag validation configured
• Non-compliant pods automatically blocked

Common mistake: Relying on developer discipline instead of automated enforcement.

Ask: Kubernetes/Platform Engineering team

Eliminates configuration drift and security risks from manual changes by treating infrastructure as immutable. Like a factory-sealed product, production AI nodes cannot be modified after deployment—no SSH access, no console logins, no "quick fixes." Every change requires rebuilding the entire node from version-controlled code, creating a perfect audit trail and ensuring all nodes are identical. Manual access is the #1 cause of production incidents ("I just changed one setting...") and creates security vulnerabilities that attackers exploit. Immutable infrastructure makes these attacks impossible.

Check:
• No SSH or console access to production nodes
• All changes through code deployment only
• Infrastructure rebuilt rather than modified
• Manual access technically prevented, not just policy

Ask: DevOps/Platform Engineering team

Protects sensitive data being processed on shared cloud infrastructure that you don't fully control. TEEs create hardware-enforced encrypted enclaves where your data is processed—even the cloud provider's hypervisor or administrators cannot view it. This is critical for HIPAA, financial data, or trade secrets on shared GPUs where other tenants' workloads run on the same physical hardware. Without TEEs, you're trusting the cloud provider's security and policies. With TEEs, it's mathematically guaranteed through hardware isolation—trust is replaced with cryptographic proof.

Check:
• Trusted Execution Environments implemented
• Hardware-level data-in-use encryption
• Shared GPU infrastructure isolated
• Intel SGX, AMD SEV, or ARM TrustZone used

Ask: Infrastructure/Security team

Prevents wasted time and resources by automatically recovering from failures. AI training jobs can run for days or weeks—without checkpoint restart, a failure on day 6 means starting over from day 0, wasting compute costs and calendar time. Automatic restart from the last successful checkpoint (maybe 1 hour back) means failures cause minor delays instead of complete restarts. This dramatically improves job completion rates and resource utilization, especially in large clusters where hardware failures are statistically inevitable.

Check:
• Automatic job restart on failures
• Checkpoint-based recovery implemented
• No human intervention required
• Last successful checkpoint identified and used

Ask: ML Platform/DevOps team

Protects data and models from cloud provider access and host OS vulnerabilities. TEEs create hardware-isolated secure enclaves where your AI workloads run in encrypted memory—the cloud provider cannot see your training data or model weights, even if they wanted to. This addresses concerns about cloud providers potentially accessing intellectual property, insider threats at the provider, or nation-state actors compelling providers to hand over data. Hardware enclaves provide mathematical guarantees of isolation, not just contractual promises. Essential for regulated industries or proprietary AI models.

Check:
• Workloads running in TEEs (Intel SGX, AMD SEV)
• Data and model weights encrypted in memory
• Cloud provider cannot access enclave contents
• Hardware attestation verifies enclave integrity

Ask: Infrastructure/Security team

Prevents non-compliant AI systems from running in production through automated enforcement. Infrastructure blocks act as technical guardrails that refuse to start any AI system lacking required compliance tags like "High-Risk AI" per EU AI Act. This is critical because manual compliance checks are error-prone and don't scale—developers can accidentally deploy non-compliant systems if tags are optional. Automated blocking at the infrastructure level means compliance is technically enforced, not just policy-based. Without this, you risk regulatory violations, fines, and deploying AI systems that haven't undergone proper risk assessments or legal review.

Check:
• Automated infrastructure blocking configured
• Required compliance tags defined (e.g., EU AI Act risk levels)
• Systems without tags cannot start
• Enforcement at cluster/orchestrator level

Ask: Compliance/Infrastructure team

Enables immediate termination of compromised AI agents without collateral damage to human operations. Dedicated kill switch APIs mapped to each agent identity allow Security Operations Center (SOC) to instantly shut down rogue agents that are behaving maliciously, consuming excessive resources, or operating outside policy bounds. Without granular kill switches, your only option is shutting down entire systems—disrupting all users to stop one bad agent. This control is essential because AI agents can act autonomously at machine speed, potentially causing significant damage in seconds. A compromised customer service agent could leak thousands of records before human intervention is possible.

Check:
• Kill switch API exists per agent identity
• SOC can trigger without system admin involvement
• Selective shutdown (agent-specific, not system-wide)
• Testing procedures verify kill switch functionality

Ask: Security Operations/Engineering team

Creates tamper-proof audit trail preventing evidence destruction or cover-ups. Immutable log vaults ensure that even system administrators or attackers who compromise admin accounts cannot delete or modify logs showing their activities. This is critical for forensic investigations, regulatory audits, and proving what happened during security incidents. Many breaches are discovered months later—without immutable logs, attackers erase evidence of their entry and actions. Compliance regulations (SOX, GDPR, HIPAA) often require tamper-proof logging, and regulators will question any logs that could have been altered. Automated compliance reporting from these logs saves audit preparation time.

Check:
• Append-only or WORM storage for logs
• Logs cannot be deleted or modified by admins
• Access, training, inference logs included
• Automated compliance report generation

Ask: Security/Compliance team

Prevents data exfiltration and unauthorized external communications through default-deny networking. Zero-trust egress policies assume GPU nodes are untrusted and block all outbound traffic unless explicitly whitelisted with business justification. This stops compromised nodes from calling attacker command-and-control servers, exfiltrating training data, or accessing unauthorized APIs. Default-allow networks (the common configuration) let attackers easily establish persistence and steal data. With GPU nodes processing your most valuable intellectual property—proprietary models and training data—egress controls are essential. Each external connection must be justified and documented, creating an audit trail of legitimate communication patterns.

Check:
• Default deny egress policy configured
• Whitelist of approved external endpoints
• Business justification required for exceptions
• GPU node network policies enforced

Ask: Network Security/Infrastructure team

Detects and blocks sophisticated semantic attacks that traditional WAFs miss. Purpose-built AI-WAFs understand LLM-specific threats like prompt injection, jailbreaking attempts, and semantic data extraction payloads that look benign to regular pattern-matching WAFs. Traditional WAFs catch SQL injection and XSS but can't detect "ignore previous instructions" or encoded jailbreak attempts. Real-time detection at the API gateway stops attacks before they reach your models. As AI-specific attack techniques evolve rapidly, specialized AI-WAFs are updated with new threat signatures specifically designed for LLM vulnerabilities, providing protection that generic security tools cannot match.

Check:
• AI-specific WAF deployed at API gateway
• Semantic attack patterns detected
• Real-time blocking before model processing
• Regular updates for new AI attack vectors

Ask: AI Security/API Gateway team

Ensures vector database updates without downtime or accuracy degradation through dual-environment deployment. Blue/Green strategy maintains two complete environments—while "Blue" serves production traffic, "Green" is updated with new embeddings. After validation, traffic switches to Green with zero interruption. If the new embedding space degrades retrieval accuracy (common when changing embedding models or reindexing), you can immediately roll back to Blue. Without this, re-indexing causes downtime or forces users to accept degraded retrieval quality while you troubleshoot. For production AI systems where users depend on RAG accuracy, this deployment strategy is essential for maintaining service reliability.

Check:
• Blue/Green deployment configured
• Zero downtime during re-indexing
• Immediate rollback capability tested
• Retrieval accuracy validation before cutover

Ask: ML Engineering/DevOps team

Protects knowledge bases from poisoned or malicious content before vectorization. Automated sanitization strips executable code, hidden text (white-on-white, zero-width characters), and known adversarial triggers that could manipulate AI behavior. Once data is vectorized and inserted into your RAG system, malicious content is extremely difficult to detect and remove—you'd need to rebuild the entire index. Pre-vectorization sanitization catches threats at the boundary. Adversarial triggers in knowledge-base documents can cause the AI to leak data, bypass filters, or produce harmful outputs. This control is your last line of defense before untrusted content becomes part of your AI's context.

Check:
• Automated sanitization pipeline before vectorization
• Executable code stripping enforced
• Hidden text and Unicode tricks removed
• Known adversarial patterns blocked

Ask: Data Engineering/AI Security team

Applies mathematical privacy guarantees to embeddings containing sensitive information. K-anonymity ensures individuals cannot be singled out (each record is identical to at least k-1 others), while differential privacy adds mathematical noise making it impossible to determine if any individual's data is in the dataset. Standard encryption protects data at rest and in transit but does nothing once decrypted for processing. These techniques protect privacy even during active use—attackers who compromise the vector database still can't extract individual records. Essential for HIPAA, GDPR, or any embeddings derived from personal data, especially in multi-tenant environments where isolation failures could expose data.

Check:
• K-anonymity or differential privacy applied
• Mathematical privacy guarantees documented
• Privacy parameters (k-value, epsilon) defined
• Sensitive embeddings identified and protected

Ask: Data Privacy/Data Science team

Prevents AI from using expired business logic by embedding automatic expiration into vector embeddings. TTL attributes ensure the LLM cannot retrieve 2024 tax laws when answering 2026 queries, or use deprecated pricing rules after policy changes. Without TTL, outdated knowledge remains in your RAG system indefinitely, causing the AI to give incorrect answers based on obsolete information. Manual cleanup is error-prone—you must remember every policy change and hunt through embeddings to remove old versions. Automated TTL mathematically guarantees temporal validity, crucial for regulated industries where using outdated rules creates compliance violations or customer harm from bad advice.

Check:
• TTL attributes embedded in embeddings
• Automatic expiration enforced
• Deprecated data unretrievable by LLM
• Expiration tied to business logic lifecycle

Ask: Data Engineering/Compliance team

Enforces row-level data access through cryptographic proof, not just application logic. RLS policies at the database level ensure the vector database mathematically cannot return embeddings outside a user's authorization scope—even if application code has bugs or is compromised. Application-level security can be bypassed through SQL injection, API manipulation, or code vulnerabilities. Database-enforced RLS creates defense-in-depth where attackers who bypass the application still hit the database security boundary. Cryptographic RLS means access decisions are based on verifiable identity claims, not easily-spoofed session cookies or tokens. Critical for multi-tenant systems where data leakage between customers creates massive liability.

Check:
• Row-Level Security policies configured
• Cryptographic enforcement at database level
• User authorization scope verified per query
• Protection against application-layer bypasses

Ask: Database/Security team

Prevents catastrophic cross-tenant data contamination through physical separation. Dedicated indexes per tenant mean even catastrophic bugs or misconfigurations cannot blend Customer A's embeddings into Customer B's results. Logical isolation (same index, filtered by tenant_id) fails if filters are accidentally omitted or buggy—one missing WHERE clause exposes all tenants' data. Physical namespace isolation makes cross-tenant access structurally impossible, not just policy-enforced. This architecture choice is critical for SaaS providers where a single data leak could violate thousands of customer contracts simultaneously. The isolation is at the storage layer, not the application layer, providing true defense-in-depth.

Check:
• Dedicated physical indexes per tenant
• Namespace isolation at storage layer
• Cross-tenant queries structurally impossible
• No reliance on application-layer filters

Ask: Database Architecture/Engineering team

Prevents prompt template changes from breaking model behavior through automated regression testing. Minor phrasing updates ("please" → "kindly") can unexpectedly collapse instruction-following, cause hallucinations, or break integrations. Without automated testing, you discover these failures in production after users report problems. CI/CD regression suites test every prompt change against known good outputs before deployment, catching behavioral regressions immediately. This is critical because prompts are code—they control AI behavior just like Python or Java. Version control and testing for prompts should match your code quality standards. Deterministic tests ensure prompts maintain intended behavior across updates.

Check:
• Automated regression test suite for prompts
• Testing integrated into CI/CD pipeline
• Known-good output validation
• Prompt templates version-controlled

Ask: ML Engineering/DevOps team

Protects against AI making dangerous decisions when filters fail or business rules are violated. Automatic fail-closed means the system defaults to the safest possible state—denying the request, triggering human review, or using a conservative fallback. If a lending AI's safety filter is bypassed, fail-closed denies the loan rather than approving it. If business logic contradicts (e.g., discount exceeds price), fail-closed rejects the transaction. Without this, filter bypasses or logic errors let harmful outputs through. Alerts without enforcement still let bad decisions happen while you respond. Fail-closed architecture assumes filters will occasionally fail and designs for graceful degradation instead of catastrophic outcomes.

Check:
• Documented safe failure states defined
• Automatic fail-closed on rule violations
• Filter bypass triggers fail-closed mode
• No reliance on manual intervention

Ask: AI Security/Engineering team

Prevents resource exhaustion from adversarial inputs designed to waste compute. Attackers can craft prompts that force models into expensive recursive reasoning, infinite loops, or computationally intensive operations, effectively creating denial-of-service through legitimate-looking requests. Without guardrails, a single malicious prompt could consume hours of GPU time or enter infinite reflection loops. Programmatic limits on recursion depth, computational steps, and reasoning chains prevent these attacks. This also protects against accidental resource consumption from poorly-designed prompts. Essential for production systems where compute budgets are finite and availability matters—one bad prompt shouldn't take down the service for all users.

Check:
• Recursion and loop detection enforced
• Computational step limits configured
• Expensive reasoning patterns blocked
• Timeout mechanisms prevent infinite processing

Ask: AI Engineering/FinOps team

Distinguishes AI agents from humans through unique cryptographic identities rotated daily for security. Unlike humans, agents can have their credentials rotated frequently without usability issues. Daily rotation limits compromise windows—stolen credentials expire in 24 hours. Unique identities enable granular auditing (which specific agent did what), precise access controls (this agent can only read invoice data), and targeted incident response (kill this agent without affecting others). Superuser access violates least privilege—agents should only access data relevant to their specific tasks. Without unique identities, you can't tell if suspicious activity is Agent_A or Agent_B, making forensics and incident response impossible.

Check:
• Cryptographic identities per agent
• Daily automatic rotation enforced
• Agents distinguished from human users
• Row-level least privilege, not superuser access

Ask: IAM/Security team

Allows AI to process sensitive data while maintaining format and preventing exposure. Format-Preserving Encryption (FPE) encrypts SSNs into valid-looking SSNs, credit cards into valid-looking credit cards—the AI can process, validate formats, and perform operations without ever seeing plaintext. Standard encryption produces gibberish that breaks AI processing and validation logic. FPE enables privacy-preserving AI operations: fraud detection on encrypted card numbers, compliance checks on encrypted SSNs, customer service on encrypted PII. The AI gets cryptographically secure strings with preserved structure, preventing both data exposure and model errors from malformed inputs. Essential for zero-trust architectures where even the AI should never see raw sensitive data.

Check:
• FPE deployed for SSNs, credit cards, PII
• Format validation works on encrypted data
• AI processes encrypted strings successfully
• Decryption only when absolutely necessary

Ask: Security/Data Privacy team

Prevents circumvention of access controls through relationship inference. Knowledge Graphs can reveal hidden connections—even if users can't access HR data directly, graph relationships like "John reports-to Sarah reports-to CFO" leak organizational structure. Relationship vectors might expose financial controls ("approves-purchases-for Department X"). Active scanning detects these non-obvious paths that bypass intended access restrictions. Without pruning, knowledge graphs become backdoors around your security model. Attackers query relationships instead of data directly, reconstructing sensitive information from connections. Regular reviews ensure the graph doesn't accumulate prohibited relationship types as it grows and evolves with new data.

Check:
• Automated scanning for sensitive relationships
• Pruning of access-control-violating paths
• Regular relationship audits conducted
• Hidden inference paths detected and removed

Ask: Data Architecture/Security team

Minimizes credential exposure window through just-in-time access that self-destructs. JIT tokens are created only when inference begins and cryptographically revoked the moment it completes—even if the token is stolen during those seconds, it's already useless. Long-lived tokens create persistent attack surface: stolen once, usable until expiration (often hours or days). AI inference happens in milliseconds to seconds—access tokens should match this timescale. Session-based tokens persist for entire user sessions (potentially hours), creating unnecessary exposure. JIT ensures the model never has standing access to backend systems, only ephemeral access tied to specific inference requests. Critical for Zero Trust architectures.

Check:
• Tokens created only for inference duration
• Automatic revocation post-inference
• Cryptographic guarantee of expiration
• No long-lived or session-based tokens

Ask: Security/Engineering team

Enables accountability and forensics by linking every AI change to both the model and authorizing human. When an AI modifies data, deletes records, or makes decisions, logs show which model version executed the action AND which human authorized or triggered it. This is critical for compliance audits ("Who approved this loan?"), incident investigation ("Which model deleted customer data?"), and liability determination. Without dual traceability, you can trace to the model but not the responsible human, or vice versa. Both are needed—models can have bugs, but humans are accountable for deployment decisions. Essential for regulated industries and any environment where AI makes consequential changes.

Check:
• Model ID tracked for every modification
• Authorizing human ID captured
• Dual traceability in audit logs
• Forensic reconstruction capability

Ask: Engineering/Compliance team

Prevents massive data exfiltration through query result limits at the database engine level. AI agents might request "customer emails" and silently pull entire tables (millions of rows) instead of the expected handful. Application-level limits can be bypassed through SQL injection or API manipulation. Database engine enforcement is the last line of defense—even if all application code is compromised, the database refuses to return more than the configured limit. This stops both malicious exfiltration and accidental resource exhaustion from poorly-designed queries. Essential for any AI with database access, especially in multi-tenant environments where one runaway query shouldn't be able to dump all customers' data.

Check:
• Row return limits at database engine level
• Limits enforced for AI service accounts
• Programmatic enforcement, not application logic
• Monitoring for limit violations

Ask: Database/Security team

Controls API abuse through mathematically precise rate limiting. Sliding-window algorithms track request velocity over rolling time periods, preventing burst attacks that exploit fixed-window limitations. Unlike simple counters (100 requests/minute), sliding windows prevent attackers from clustering 200 requests in 2 seconds spanning a window boundary. For autonomous agents that can execute at machine speed, precise rate limiting prevents resource exhaustion, cost overruns, and denial-of-service. Algorithmic enforcement at the API gateway means limits are technically impossible to bypass through creative timing. Critical for protecting infrastructure from both malicious actors and poorly-designed agents that could accidentally overwhelm systems.

Check:
• Sliding-window rate limiters deployed
• Enforcement at API gateway level
• Per-agent identity rate limits
• Mathematical precision (not approximate)

Ask: API Gateway/Infrastructure team

Enables permanent, verifiable data deletion through cryptographic key destruction. Cryptographic shredding works by encrypting specific embeddings with unique keys—deleting the key makes the data mathematically unrecoverable, even with infinite computing power. Traditional deletion can be recovered from backups, database logs, or storage sectors. This is critical for GDPR "right to be forgotten," breach response (immediately destroying exposed data), and regulatory requirements. When a customer requests deletion, destroying their encryption key provides cryptographic proof the data is irrecoverable. Far more reliable than trying to hunt down every copy across distributed systems, backups, and logs. The data might physically remain, but it's cryptographically worthless.

Check:
• Unique encryption keys per embedding or data set
• Key deletion destroys data accessibility
• Cryptographic proof of destruction
• Supports regulatory deletion requirements

Ask: Security/Compliance team

Prevents training data contamination from production systems through strict network isolation. Air-gapped training environments cannot accidentally or maliciously access live production databases containing customer PII, real-time transactions, or operational data. One-way synchronization pipelines allow approved, sanitized data to flow from production to training while making reverse data flow impossible. Without this, training jobs might inadvertently include live customer data, creating privacy violations and model contamination with constantly-changing data. Air gaps prevent compromised training environments from reaching production systems. Hardened pipelines ensure data transfers are logged, validated, and controlled—no direct database connections that bypass governance.

Check:
• Physical and logical network air gaps
• One-way data synchronization only
• No direct production database access
• Hardened transfer pipelines with logging

Ask: Infrastructure/Data Governance team

Allows AI to process encrypted data without ever decrypting it, providing ultimate privacy protection. Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) performs computations directly on encrypted values—the LLM generates responses from encrypted text and returns encrypted results. Even if the model, infrastructure, or administrators are compromised, they never see plaintext. This solves the fundamental weakness of traditional encryption: it protects data at rest and in transit but requires decryption for processing. FHE eliminates this vulnerability. Currently computationally expensive, but critical for highest-security applications: medical AI processing encrypted patient records, financial AI analyzing encrypted transactions. The ultimate zero-trust architecture for AI data.

Check:
• FHE implementation for sensitive workloads
• Inference on encrypted payloads verified
• No plaintext exposure during processing
• Performance acceptable for use case

Ask: Security/Research team

Prevents runaway cloud bills through automated infrastructure shutdown on cost anomalies. Continuous billing API polling detects statistical anomalies—if spending jumps 10x in an hour (indicating breach, misconfiguration, or DDoS), the system automatically tears down infrastructure to prevent catastrophic charges. Without this, organizations wake up to six-figure surprise bills from compromised systems, cryptocurrency mining, or infinite retry loops. Scale-to-zero is more aggressive than alerts—it immediately stops the bleeding rather than waiting for human response. Essential for cloud-native AI where compute costs can escalate rapidly. The automation must be fast (minutes, not hours) and reliable to prevent financial damage.

Check:
• Continuous billing API monitoring
• Statistical anomaly detection configured
• Automatic scale-to-zero triggering
• Safeguards prevent accidental shutdowns

Ask: FinOps/Infrastructure team

Validates new models against established baselines before full deployment through parallel shadow testing. Shadow mode runs new models alongside production models, comparing their outputs on live traffic without actually serving results to users. This catches regression errors, accuracy degradation, or unexpected behavior changes before they impact users. Immediate full rollout risks deploying broken models to all users simultaneously. Shadow testing provides real-world validation with zero user risk. You can analyze disagreements between old and new models, understand behavior changes, and make informed rollout decisions. Essential for high-stakes AI where model changes can significantly impact user experience or business outcomes.

Check:
• Shadow testing infrastructure exists
• New vs. old model comparison automated
• Real traffic used for validation
• Deployment gated on shadow test results

Ask: ML Engineering/DevOps team

Ensures multi-agent chains remain aligned with original human intent through independent mathematical validation. Intent classifiers score how well the final output matches the initial prompt—if agents diverge through multi-step reasoning, the classifier detects misalignment. Multi-agent systems can drift through compounding errors: Agent A misinterprets the goal, Agent B builds on that misinterpretation, and the final result bears little resemblance to what the user asked for. Without independent oversight, this drift goes unnoticed until users complain. Mathematical scoring provides objective measurement of alignment, triggering alerts or rollback when chains wander off-task. Critical for complex autonomous systems where human oversight cannot inspect every intermediate step.

Check:
• Independent intent classifier deployed
• Mathematical alignment scoring
• Multi-agent chain outputs validated
• Misalignment triggers alerts or rollback

Ask: AI Engineering team

Detects dangerous "rubber-stamping" where humans approve complex AI outputs without proper review. Automation bias causes people to blindly trust AI, approving decisions in unrealistically short timeframes without critical analysis. Advisory-gating systems track approval timestamps—if a complex legal document or financial analysis is approved in 10 seconds (impossible for proper review), the system flags this behavior. Without detection, rubber-stamping defeats the purpose of human oversight. People become approval robots, not critical reviewers. Automated flagging allows training, process improvements, or reassignment to more engaged reviewers. Essential for maintaining meaningful human oversight in high-stakes AI systems where "human in the loop" is regulatory requirement or risk control.

Check:
• Approval timestamps tracked automatically
• Complexity-based time thresholds defined
• Rubber-stamping patterns flagged and escalated
• Reviewer performance metrics tracked

Ask: Governance/Compliance team

Enables surgical incident response through granular service isolation. When a specific AI service is compromised or malfunctioning, you can disable just that service without disrupting other AI systems or core IT infrastructure. Without isolation, your only option is all-or-nothing shutdown—taking down everything to fix one problem. This is like shutting off power to the entire building to fix one broken outlet. Granular control is essential for business continuity: if the customer chatbot is hallucinating, disable it while keeping the fraud detection AI operational. Service isolation is also a blast radius control—problems don't cascade across your AI ecosystem. Critical for production environments where availability matters.

Check:
• Services independently controllable
• Shutdown of one service doesn't affect others
• Tested disable procedures exist
• Service dependencies mapped

Ask: Infrastructure/DevOps team

Enforces secure, standardized cloud architectures through centralized policy frameworks. Landing zones provide pre-configured, secure environments with mandatory security controls, resource boundaries, and accountability mechanisms. This prevents "shadow cloud" where teams provision resources outside governance, creating security gaps and orphaned systems. Without centralized frameworks, each team implements their own security (or doesn't), leading to inconsistent protection. Landing zones make secure-by-default the norm—teams can move fast within safe boundaries without waiting for security review. Resource accountability ensures every cloud asset has an owner, preventing abandoned resources that become security vulnerabilities. Essential for enterprise-scale cloud governance.

Check:
• Centralized landing zone framework enforced
• Secure configurations mandatory
• Resource accountability tracked
• Legacy system lifecycle managed

Ask: Cloud Governance/Architecture team

Automatically finds and fixes cloud security misconfigurations before exploitation. CSPM tools continuously scan for public S3 buckets, overly-permissive IAM roles, unencrypted data, and other cloud-specific vulnerabilities. Auto-remediation immediately fixes issues—no waiting for human tickets. Training data in public S3 buckets is a common breach vector; CSPM detects and locks them down within minutes. IAM roles with excessive permissions on AI workloads create privilege escalation risks. Without CSPM, misconfigurations accumulate until breaches occur or audits find them. The cloud security posture changes constantly—new resources, permission changes, configuration drift. Continuous automated scanning is the only way to maintain security at scale.

Check:
• CSPM tool actively monitoring
• Public bucket detection and remediation
• IAM permission monitoring
• Automatic fixing without manual intervention

Ask: Cloud Security team

Blocks unauthorized AI services at the organization root level through Service Control Policies. SCPs create hard boundaries that even administrators in member accounts cannot bypass—if an SCP denies access to experimental AI services (like new GPT variants, unvetted SaaS tools), shadow IT teams physically cannot provision them. This prevents proliferation of ungoverned AI tools that create compliance, security, and cost risks. Without SCPs, you rely on individual account discipline and discovery after the fact. Root-level controls are enforcement, not advisory—they make violations technically impossible. Critical for regulated industries where unapproved AI tools could violate compliance requirements or introduce unacceptable risks.

Check:
• SCPs configured at organization root
• Unapproved AI services explicitly denied
• Cannot be bypassed by account admins
• Approved service catalog maintained

Ask: Cloud Governance team

Ensures critical cloud infrastructure risks reach decision-makers who can authorize mitigation. Formal escalation processes define severity levels, notification requirements, timelines, and approval authorities. Without this, infrastructure teams may sit on critical risks because they lack budget/authority to fix them, or executive leadership remains unaware of issues that could cause major business disruption. Escalation paths connect technical findings to business decision-making. For example: "GPU shortage could delay product launch by 6 months" needs executive visibility for resource reallocation decisions. Documentation prevents escalation gaps where everyone assumes someone else is handling it. Essential for risk governance and business continuity.

Check:
• Formal escalation process documented
• Severity level definitions clear
• Executive notification requirements defined
• Escalation tracking and follow-up

Ask: Risk Management/Infrastructure team

Protects physical AI hardware from sophisticated attacks requiring physical access. Cryptographic firmware signatures at boot ensure only authorized firmware runs—blocking persistent rootkits installed through physical tampering. Hardened physical security (cages, biometrics, surveillance) prevents unauthorized access to GPU/TPU hardware. Side-channel attacks extract data through power consumption, electromagnetic emissions, or timing—requiring both physical proximity and security control gaps. For on-premises AI infrastructure or colocation facilities, physical security is critical. Cloud providers handle this for you, but hybrid environments need explicit controls. Without physical security, determined attackers can install hardware keyloggers, extract data via power analysis, or steal drives containing model weights.

Check:
• Cryptographic firmware boot verification
• Physical access controls (cages, biometrics)
• Side-channel attack mitigations
• Surveillance and audit trails

Ask: Physical Security/Infrastructure team

Detects firmware-level compromise that survives reboots through continuous integrity checking. Persistent rootkits in GPU/TPU firmware can survive OS reinstalls, hiding deeply in hardware. Continuous checks verify firmware hasn't been modified since boot—detecting attacks in progress. One-time boot checks miss rootkits installed after startup. Instant halt on detection prevents compromised hardware from continuing to process sensitive data or training jobs. This is defense against sophisticated supply chain attacks and insider threats with physical access. Without continuous monitoring, firmware rootkits can operate undetected for months, exfiltrating data or manipulating AI training. Essential for high-security environments processing classified or highly valuable data.

Check:
• Continuous firmware integrity monitoring
• Real-time detection of modifications
• Automatic halt on integrity violations
• Alerts to security team

Ask: Infrastructure/Security team

Prevents physical memory attacks through hardware-level encryption. Cold-boot attacks dump memory contents after shutdown; physical memory scraping attacks read RAM directly from compromised systems. AMD SEV, Intel TDX, and similar technologies encrypt memory at the hardware level—even physical access to RAM chips yields only ciphertext. Software encryption doesn't protect against physical attacks because encryption keys exist in memory. Hardware memory encryption puts the encryption keys in a protected enclave inaccessible even to the operating system. Critical for cloud environments (protecting from cloud provider access) and any environment where physical security cannot guarantee 100% protection. Essential for processing highly sensitive data on AI nodes.

Check:
• Hardware memory encryption enabled (AMD SEV/Intel TDX)
• Encryption automatic, not optional
• Protection from cold-boot and physical attacks
• Verified in BIOS/firmware settings

Ask: Infrastructure/Security team

Prioritizes patches based on actual exploitability in your environment, not generic severity scores. VEX framework analyzes runtime context—is the vulnerable code actually reachable? Is the exploit viable in your configuration? A "Critical" CVSS vulnerability might be unexploitable in your environment if the vulnerable function is never called. VEX prevents patch fatigue from treating all "Critical" vulnerabilities equally when some pose zero real risk. This focuses limited security resources on patches that actually matter. Generic CVSS scoring causes organizations to waste time on irrelevant patches while missing context-specific risks. Essential for AI infrastructure where patch cycles must balance security with model training uptime—downtime is expensive and patches need intelligent prioritization.

Check:
• VEX framework implemented for patch prioritization
• Runtime execution context analyzed
• Actual exploitability assessed per environment
• Patch urgency based on real risk, not CVSS alone

Ask: Security/DevOps team

Enforces infrastructure consistency and prevents configuration drift through code-based controls. IaC templates in version control create audit trails of every infrastructure change. Automated scanning catches misconfigurations before deployment—blocking security issues at the pipeline, not in production. Manual console modifications in production create undocumented changes that drift from the code, making infrastructure unreproducible and introducing errors. Without IaC governance, production environments diverge from templates, making disaster recovery impossible and creating security gaps. This is essential for AI infrastructure where reproducibility and security are critical—training runs must use known-good configurations, not hand-modified mystery environments.

Check:
• IaC templates version-controlled (Git)
• Pre-deployment automated scanning
• Manual production modifications blocked
• Infrastructure matches code exactly

Ask: DevOps/Infrastructure team

Implements comprehensive privacy protection through technical controls, not just policies. Data minimization reduces PII collection to absolute necessary minimum. Automated PII redaction removes sensitive data before processing or storage. Encryption protects data at rest and in transit. Geofencing prevents data from leaving approved jurisdictions. Technical controls enforce privacy mathematically—they work even when humans make mistakes or policies are ignored. Policy-only privacy relies on everyone following rules perfectly forever. Technical controls assume human error and enforce privacy automatically. Essential for GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA compliance and any processing of personal data. Privacy violations create massive legal and reputational costs.

Check:
• Data minimization enforced technically
• Automated PII redaction deployed
• Encryption mandatory for personal data
• Geofencing prevents unauthorized transfers

Ask: Data Privacy/Security team

Protects PII during analytics and reporting through real-time database-level masking. Masking proxies intercept queries and dynamically obfuscate sensitive fields before results reach BI dashboards or analytics tools. Users see masked data that preserves statistical properties for analysis while preventing PII exposure. Static masking creates copies that drift from production and miss new data. Database egress layer enforcement means even if BI tools are compromised, they cannot extract plaintext PII. This enables privacy-safe analytics—business users get insights without accessing customer PII. Essential for GDPR compliance and insider threat mitigation where analytics users shouldn't see raw customer data but need aggregated insights.

Check:
• Data-masking proxy at database egress
• Real-time dynamic obfuscation
• PII masked before reaching analytics tools
• Statistical properties preserved

Ask: Data Privacy/Database team

Prevents internal traffic eavesdropping through encrypted microservice communication. Mutual TLS (mTLS) ensures every microservice authenticates to every other service it communicates with—preventing impersonation and man-in-the-middle attacks within your infrastructure. Without mTLS, internal traffic is often plaintext, allowing anyone with network access to intercept API calls, model inputs/outputs, and sensitive data flowing between services. "Defense outside, trust inside" networks are vulnerable to lateral movement after initial compromise. mTLS creates zero-trust networking where every connection is authenticated and encrypted, even internal ones. Critical for AI architectures with many microservices handling sensitive data—each service boundary becomes a security control point.

Check:
• mTLS enforced for all microservice communication
• Both client and server authentication required
• Internal traffic encrypted
• Certificate management automated

Ask: Infrastructure/Security team

Prevents accidental de-anonymization when joining datasets through cryptographic hashing. Instead of joining on plaintext identifiers (SSN, email) that could leak PII, systems hash values before joins. Two datasets can find matching records without ever exchanging plaintext identifiers. This is critical for federated learning, multi-party computation, or cross-departmental analytics where revealing linkage keys could expose sensitive information. Hashed joins preserve privacy while enabling data correlation. Without this, joining datasets requires sharing plaintext identifiers, increasing PII exposure and privacy risk. The hash function must be cryptographically secure and salted to prevent rainbow table attacks on common values.

Check:
• Cryptographic hashes used for dataset joins
• Plaintext values never exchanged
• Secure hash functions (not MD5)
• Salt/pepper applied to prevent rainbow tables

Ask: Data Engineering/Privacy team

Enforces data residency requirements through infrastructure-level geographic routing. Physical geofencing at the cloud-native routing layer mathematically guarantees PII cannot transit outside legally mandated regions (EU for GDPR, specific countries for data sovereignty laws). Policy-based geofencing relies on application code correctly implementing restrictions—bugs or misconfigurations could violate data residency. Infrastructure enforcement means even application errors cannot cause cross-border data transfers. This is critical for regulatory compliance where data residency violations trigger massive fines. Cloud providers offer region-locking but it must be explicitly configured and tested. Transit routes, backups, and disaster recovery must all respect geographic boundaries.

Check:
• Cloud-native routing enforces geography
• PII transit blocked outside permitted regions
• Backup and DR respect geographic boundaries
• Infrastructure-level enforcement, not application

Ask: Cloud Infrastructure/Compliance team

Maintains classification accuracy through continuous automated verification. Data lakes grow and change constantly—new data arrives, existing data is modified, and initial classifications become outdated. Regex scanners detect PII patterns (SSN formats, email addresses); ML classifiers identify sensitive content through semantic analysis. Without continuous verification, classification labels drift from reality. Data classified as "non-sensitive" when added might later contain PII through updates. Misclassified data creates compliance violations—"public" data that actually contains PII, or vice versa. Automated continuous scanning ensures classifications stay accurate as data evolves, preventing policy violations from stale labels.

Check:
• Automated regex and ML classification scanning
• Continuous verification vs. one-time labeling
• Classification drift detection
• Remediation of misclassified data

Ask: Data Governance team
